verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same formula after the substitution y' = log(s/q): Lean integrates in the physical variable s over Ioi s0 with measure ds/s, which is exactly dy'; the prefactor 2η/(q^D L) is packaged as logScaleDerivative h p (unfolding qAxial gives 2ηq/(q^D L) divided by q). Two encoding choices: (i) Lean's upper limit is +∞ where the paper writes 3 — the two agree because f' vanishes beyond the plateau y'=3, but the Lean statement does not itself record that truncation, so the identity with the paper's finite integral needs that vanishing; (ii) Lean writes the heat factor as physicalHeat C (1+h) rather than K(y'), the same quantity in the physical variable.
